title: CBA faces $3b pre-listing dilemma
full_text:
Commonwealth Bank is unlikely to use Anthropic's float to sell its near-$3 billion stake and rake in huge gains, despite recording a stunning return on what started as a small venture capital-like bet.
That is the view of Australian bank analysts, some of whom expect notable Anthropic investors to be bound by escrow periods or say CBA will want to retain some exposure to the AI behemoth at a float that could value it at up to $US2 trillion ($2.8 trillion).
Anthropic's prospectus for its initial public offering mentioned larger investors, including Amazon and Google, but did not outline the size of the IPO raising, the price of securities or any sell-down by existing holders.
CBA's unlisted equity investment in Anthropic had a carrying value of more than $1.5 billion at June 30 - up 10-times from just $153 million a year earlier.
CBA's latest valuation was based on an Anthropic capital raising in May, when the company tapped investors for $US65 billion at a $US965 billion valuation. The bank did not participate in that round.
The investment by the Matt Comyn-led bank came about in March last year as it sought to align with Anthropic and access to the most advanced AI models, technology and engineering expertise.
A CBA spokesman declined to comment on Tuesday about the bank's plans for the holding.
MST Marquee analyst Brian Johnson expects CBA will not be able to offload its stake as part of Anthropic's IPO. "It's reasonable to expect CommBank can't just sell its shares into the IPO. I am suspecting they will be locked out of selling," he said. "The relationship with Anthropic probably goes beyond the notional investment gain and just having an equity stake."
While cautioning that details about the mooted Anthropic IPO were still to come, including the issuance of shares to staff and any dilution in CBA's stake due to a convertible note, Johnson estimated the bank stood to make a paper gain of $2.8 billion on its initial investment.
That is based on CBA's stake being valued at $US2.07 billion if Anthropic were to raise $US100 billion, delivering it a market valuation of $US1.6 trillion to $US2 trillion.
CLSA banking analyst Ed Henning said: "The previous [CBA] playbook from Klarna shows there is a possibility that they could sell down moderately [at IPO], but they are not in desperate need of capital, so they could continue to hold on."
When Klarna, the Swedish buy now, pay later firm, listed last year, CBA sold part of its stake as part of the IPO, netting the bank about $100 million.
CBA also has a strategic relationship with OpenAI, which it has used to jointly launch an AI, cybersecurity and digital initiative for small businesses.
Jarden analyst Matt Wilson said while Comyn was an "AI enthusiast", the bank could seek to sell some of its Anthropic stake. "They may take some profit if they can, if they are allowed to. If they sold [the entire stake], it would be a very bearish signal," he said.
Investor confidence in the growth of AI and the ability of players to fund the capital-intensive technology rollout has wavered over the past three weeks. Investors baulked at supporting the proposed $44 billion valuation of float candidate Firmus Technologies and have also questioned the hefty debt levels of AI cloud platform CoreWeave.
Nine Entertainment Co.
